exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal, Cesarean section, vaginal delivery with instruments, vaginal delivery without instruments, Cesarean section prior to labor, Cesarean section during labor)
cohort: The study included 926 neonates, 786 with severe and 140 with moderate hemophilia, from a multicenter PedNet registry.
finding: Vaginal delivery and Cesarean section carry similar risks of intracranial hemorrhages and other major bleeds in neonates with moderate and severe hemophilia.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery with instruments was identified as a significant risk factor for both intracranial hemorrhages and major bleeds.
